title: Prepare molecular geometries for AM1 calculations
action: Build initial molecular geometries for all required isolated molecules (PDME, DEE, PDEE, OH, OH+, OH-, BF3, NH3) and for the complex starting structures (BF3+NH3, BF3+DEE, BF3+PDEE, OH+PDME at O site, OH++PDME at O site, OH-+PDME at C site). Write the geometries in a format readable by MOPAC (e.g., XYZ or Z-matrix) and produce a summary log file confirming the prepared input files.
description: This step ensures all necessary molecular structures are correctly built before any AM1 computation begins. The geometries are the public inputs for the semiempirical procedure.

title: Run AM1 optimizations and collect energies and distances
action: For each system listed below, perform an AM1 UHF geometry optimization (lowest spin multiplicity) using MOPAC. Record the optimized total energy in kJ/mol and the specified key interatomic distances. Systems: isolated PDME, OH, OH+, OH-, BF3, DEE, PDEE, NH3; complexes: BF3+NH3, BF3+DEE (BF3 approaching O), BF3+PDEE (BF3 approaching O), OH+PDME (neutral OH approaching ether O), OH++PDME (OH+ approaching ether O), OH-+PDME (OH- approaching a perfluoromethyl carbon). Key distances to extract: BF3-NH3 – B‑N distance; BF3-DEE – B‑O distance; BF3-PDEE – B‑O distance; OH-PDME – O(ether)–H(OH); OH+-PDME – H–O(ether) and H–O(hydroxyl); OH--PDME – O(hydroxyl)–C(ether). Write all results into a single JSON file results.json using the exact distance key names specified in the output contract.
description: All computed AM1 total energies and key interatomic distances for the 15 required systems, including validation (BF3+NH3) and target interactions.
output_schema: JSON object with top-level key 'systems' (array). Each item has 'system' (string), 'total_energy_kjmol' (number), 'key_distances' (object). For complex systems, the key_distances object MUST contain the following exact keys (case-sensitive): BF3_NH3: 'B_N'; BF3_DEE: 'B_O'; BF3_PDEE: 'B_O'; OH_PDME: 'O_ether_H_OH'; OH+_PDME: 'H_O_ether' and 'H_O_hydroxyl'; OH-_PDME: 'O_OH_C_ether'.
